lessons.claim: simbot.io.verify_seal hashed ZERO documents on all 21 archived seal directories (measured 2026-09-15 by instrumenting sha256_file). 12 returned ok=True while printing '2 documents unchanged after the run' -- summary() reported len(entries), the number of LINES in the seal file, as a verification count. The other 9 (runs/ renamed to runs_s1s8/ at the 2026-08-28 merge) returned unsealed = 'never sealed' on byte-intact content, making 'we never sealed it' and 'we sealed it then renamed the directory' the same output. Because the branch taken was unsealed and not changed, content was never read: appending a falsified prediction gave a BIT-IDENTICAL verdict. Cause: the loop iterated SEALED_STAGES (this module's filename vocabulary) instead of the seal's own entries. Undetected because every unit test seals in tmp_path where stage path == seal key, and the only test touching the archive probed runs/2026-07-28_trap-2d-5um_2dfb9d -- absent from every commit -- skipping with the false reason 'runs/ is gitignored' (git check-ignore runs exits 1; 1311 tracked files under runs/). bdbot.runcard.verify_seal was correct throughout and the broken one was the one wired to cli.py, report.py and validate.py. Fixed by iterating the seal, verifying the seal's SIBLING (the recorded path is provenance, not a resolution strategy -- following it first lets a copied run directory's seal verify the original's documents), requiring a non-empty verified list for ok, and adding a drifted field. CI's bash brought to the same rule. report.seal_check_command extracted because the advertised 'shasum -a 256 -c SEALED.sha256' resolved in NO working directory while 2 committed reports printed it beside 'seal verified'. After: 21/21 verify, 42 documents hashed, 18 drifts, two implementations agree 21/21, 5 gate mutants CAUGHT, 1434 passed / 6 skipped.
